findings.title: GitHub user check is skipped for fresh installs
findings.body: The new sender-vs-authenticated-user check is placed after the `except Integration.DoesNotExist: return pipeline.next_step()` branch (around line 481-482). When no Integration exists yet for the installation_id, the pipeline advances without comparing `github_authenticated_user` to the installing user. The PR's stated purpose is to reject a mismatch, but that case is not covered. Only the 'Integration exists but no OrganizationIntegration' path is verified.

findings.title: KeyError when integration metadata has no sender
findings.body: `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` assumes a 'sender' key. `build_integration` only stores `sender` when `state.get("sender")` is truthy, so integrations created without it (or created by other paths) will raise KeyError and produce a 500 during installation instead of the intended error page. Use `.get` with a safe fallback and fail closed.

findings.title: Authorize URL built without URL-encoding parameters
findings.body: `redirect_uri` and `state` are interpolated directly into the query string. The redirect_uri is an absolute URL with its own query/characters and is not encoded, so it can be mangled or break parsing. Build the query with urlencode to be safe.

findings.title: Brittle hard-coded responses.calls index
findings.body: The assertion switches from `responses.calls[0]` to `responses.calls[2]` to locate the JWT-authorized request. This depends on the exact number and order of mocked HTTP calls, so any change to the OAuth flow will break it for unrelated reasons. Locate the call by URL instead.
